task_instance: Given a project brief for 'OrderFlow', a mid-size retailer's online order processing platform (500 req/s peak, 99.95% availability target, 3 independently-deployed teams, EU/US data residency, RPO 5min/RTO 30min, legacy SOAP warehouse integration), produce a full architecture review and design following the skill's 7-step Architecture Review Workflow (requirements, architecture style selection, technology stack, design pattern selection, cross-cutting concerns, WAF pillar validation, and Architecture Decision Records).
evidence: Created project-brief.md (sample input requirements). Produced architecture-review.md covering all 7 workflow steps from SKILL.md: Step 1 requirements extraction, Step 2 architecture style selection (Microservices + Web-Queue-Worker + event-driven, justified against the skill's selection criteria and design principles #3/#4), Step 3 technology stack (Container Apps, Azure SQL, Cosmos DB, Service Bus, Event Grid, Front Door, Entra ID - all PaaS per principle #7), Step 4 design pattern selection (8 patterns from the skill's 44-pattern catalog: Queue-Based Load Leveling, Competing Consumers, Circuit Breaker, Retry, Bulkhead, Saga, Compensating Transaction, Publisher/Subscriber, Choreography, Anti-Corruption Layer, Strangler Fig, Static Content Hosting, Backends for Frontends, Rate Limiting, Throttling), Step 5 cross-cutting concerns (identity, monitoring, security, CI/CD), Step 6 WAF pillar validation table with explicit tradeoffs matching the skill's Tradeoff Matrix, and Step 7 three ADRs written in the skill's exact ADR-NNN template (Status/Context/Decision/Consequences) covering architecture style, order consistency pattern, and legacy integration. Verified via grep that all 7 '## Step N' headers are present in architecture-review.md and all 3 ADR files contain the required 'Status' field. This skill's core deliverable is a reasoning/document-production task (applying documented Azure architecture guidance to a concrete system design and writing it up) which required no external tools, credentials, network access, or connectors - fully achievable with local file writing.
